findings.issue_text: Dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent: the .find() predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId but only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined, causing google.events.update with calendarId: undefined and silent failure of reschedules/edits for legacy bookings
Same dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent leads to calendarId: undefined when cancelling legacy bookings, resulting in orphaned Google calendar events after cancellation
DB-fetched credential in handleCancelBooking lacks appName, so getCalendar(credential) fails to resolve the integration and calendar?.deleteEvent is a silent no-op, never deleting the calendar event

Duplicate event creation when multiple destinations lack credentialId: each destination without credentialId fans out to all matching calendarCredentials, creating the event N times for N destinations

BaseCalendarService.createEvent filter pins to first host's calendar externalId, so when called with host B's credential the filter compares against host A's externalId, creating zero events for non-first hosts' calendars in multi-host collective bookings

Team destination calendars silently dropped when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar: evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional-chained ?.push() skips adding teamDestinationCalendars
organization select removed in loadUsers non-eventTypeId branch, so downstream logic reading user.organization.slug receives undefined for dynamic-link bookings
Only destinationCalendar[0] is persisted on the Booking, so hosts 2..N lose their destination context in reschedule/cancel/email flows that reconstruct from booking.destinationCalendar
Google organizer email pinned to first host's destination externalId on every host's calendar in createEvent and updateEvent, misattributing events on non-first hosts' calendars
Recurring bulk-delete now executes once per calendar reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop instead of once, causing duplicate delete API calls, error noise, and potential rate-limiting
Calendar interface now requires a second credentialId param on createEvent; out-of-diff callers invoking calendar.createEvent(event) with one argument will fail type-checking

Google updateEvent fallback predicate searches for externalId === externalCalendarId in a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the fallback never matches and calendarId becomes undefined, breaking reschedules of legacy bookings without externalCalendarId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~253)

Google deleteEvent has the same broken fallback: when externalCalendarId is absent, calendarId is undefined instead of the destination calendar's external ID, leaving orphaned Google events when cancelling legacy bookings (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312-315)

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition in org creation: slug is now assigned directly (alongside requestedSlug) when team billing is enabled, bypassing the requested-slug review/approval gating and allowing unverified orgs to claim arbitrary slugs (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:148-151)

Reference externalId is persisted in EventResult/externalCalendarId even when Google createEvent fell back to 'primary' because no destination calendar matched the credentialId, so the stored reference points at a calendar the event was never created in, breaking later updates/deletes (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:264-266)

Credentials fetched directly from DB by ID in createAllCalendarEvents, updateEvent, and handleCancelBooking are used without validating ownership against the booking's organizer/hosts/team, creating a potential cross-tenant credential abuse primitive if credentialId ever becomes user-influenceable (packages/core/EventManager.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts)

Collective events silently drop team calendars when the organizer has no destination calendar because evt.destinationCalendar is set to null (making the later push a no-op) and team calendars are only collected for users after the first (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1062-1075)

Raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages are surfaced to clients in HTTP 400 responses in loadUsers, leaking database schema details (table/field names, constraints) on the public booking endpoint (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~750-755)

Dead fallback in Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent destination lookup: the find() only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making the destinationCalendar fallback unreachable and causing calendarId/selectedCalendar to resolve to undefined when externalCalendarId isn't supplied (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253 and :315)

Inverted boolean in org creation: slug was previously set when team billing was disabled, now it's set when team billing is enabled, flipping slug-provisioning behavior for orgs (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:150)

N+1 credential fetch plus sequential event creation loop in createAllCalendarEvents: awaiting createEvent() sequentially per destination and doing per-iteration prisma.credential.findUnique causes N sequential external calendar API calls and N individual DB round-trips on the booking-creation critical path instead of batching (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~334-385)

Same N+1 shape in updateAllCalendarEvents: sequential await prisma.credential.findUnique inside the reference.credentialId branch for every calendar reference serializes DB round-trips across references instead of batching up front (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~493-525)

Fan-out duplication when destination entries lack credentialId: every destination entry without a credentialId triggers event creation on all credentials of that integration type, so multiple destination entries lacking credentialId create duplicate calendar events and redundant API calls (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~370-376)

Stale or undefined credential leaked across reference loop iterations in updateAllCalendarEvents because credential is declared outside the for loop, causing updates to the wrong host's calendar or throwing and aborting all remaining references

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent: the .find() predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId but only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined, causing google.events.update with calendarId: undefined and silent failure of reschedules/edits for legacy bookings

adjudication.rationale:
In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, the new logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

The `.find()` branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `null`/`undefined`). In that case the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== null/undefined`), which will not match a normal calendar externalId, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` instead of falling back to the destination calendar’s externalId (as the old code did via `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). That means the update call will use an undefined calendar id (or at best lose the intended destination calendar), breaking updates for cases where `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided. The same flawed pattern is also introduced in `deleteEvent`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent leads to calendarId: undefined when cancelling legacy bookings, resulting in orphaned Google calendar events after cancellation

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now sets `calendarId` as:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null` (a plausible case for older/legacy references), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will not match any real calendar and thus returns `undefined`. That makes `calendarId` undefined even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId (the intended fallback previously was to use the event’s destination calendar). Passing an undefined `calendarId` to `calendar.events.delete` can prevent deletion and leave the external event orphaned. This is a concrete logic defect introduced by the diff; the “legacy bookings” framing is plausible given the fallback path, though the orphaning outcome depends on runtime behavior of the Google API client.

Duplicate event creation when multiple destinations lack credentialId: each destination without credentialId fans out to all matching calendarCredentials, creating the event N times for N destinations

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop iterates over every `destination` in `event.destinationCalendar`. For any `destination` without `credentialId`, it executes the `else` branch, filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration`, and then creates events for *all* matching credentials. If there are multiple destinations lacking `credentialId` (especially with the same `integration`), this fan-out happens once per destination, causing the same set of calendar credentials to receive multiple `createEvent` calls (i.e., duplicate event creation). This behavior is directly implied by the loop + fan-out logic in the diff.

[selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`, and similar in `handleCancelBooking`). The proposed finding hinges on `evt.destinationCalendar` being `null` and an optional-chained `?.push()` skipping additions of `teamDestinationCalendars`, but there is no `?.push()` (or any push) logic shown in this diff, and the modified code paths shown avoid `null` by using empty arrays. adjudication_records.issue_text: Only destinationCalendar[0] is persisted on the Booking, so hosts 2..N lose their destination context in reschedule/cancel/email flows that reconstruct from booking.destinationCalendar
Google organizer email pinned to first host's destination externalId on every host's calendar in createEvent and updateEvent, misattributing events on non-first hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the attendee marked `organizer: true` uses `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`, where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the *first* element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`. However, the actual target calendar for insertion is chosen separately via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. When events are created for multiple destination calendars (see `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` looping over `event.destinationCalendar` and calling `createEvent` per destination), the organizer email will still be taken from the first destination calendar, not the current destination being inserted. The same pattern exists in `updateEvent`, where organizer email is again derived from the first destination calendar. This is a concrete mismatch in the diff and can misattribute the organizer identity on non-first hosts' calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recurring bulk-delete now executes once per calendar reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop instead of once, causing duplicate delete API calls, error noise, and potential rate-limiting

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking, bookingCalendarReference changed from a single reference (find) to an array (filter) and is now iterated with `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that loop, the recurring bulk-delete branch builds `promises` by iterating over *all* of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and then over `updatedBookings` to call `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. That bulk-delete logic does not depend on the outer `reference` values, so it will run once per calendar reference that has a `credentialId`, duplicating the same delete calls multiple times (extra API calls/noise/rate-limit risk). Previously it could only run once because only one reference was selected via `find`.

Google updateEvent fallback predicate searches for externalId === externalCalendarId in a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the fallback never matches and calendarId becomes undefined, breaking reschedules of legacy bookings without externalCalendarId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~253)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new delete logic sets:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is absent/undefined, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will typically return no match, leaving `calendarId` undefined instead of falling back to a destination calendar’s `externalId`. This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff and can cause deletes to target the default ("primary") rather than the intended calendar, potentially leaving events orphaned.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new code paths that, when a `credentialId` is present but not found in the in-memory `this.calendarCredentials`, will fetch an arbitrary credential record directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` and then use it to create/update/delete calendar events (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateBookingReferences, handleCancelBooking). In these new fetch paths there is no validation that the fetched credential belongs to the booking’s organizer/user/team or is otherwise authorized for the operation (no check against `userId`, `teamId`, or membership). Previously, the code primarily operated on credentials already scoped in `this.calendarCredentials` / `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`; the added DB fallback bypasses that scoping. This is a real authorization gap in the diff: if an attacker can ever influence stored `destination.credentialId` or booking reference `credentialId`, the server would perform calendar operations with a credential outside the expected tenant scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent destination lookup: the find() only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making the destinationCalendar fallback unreachable and causing calendarId/selectedCalendar to resolve to undefined when externalCalendarId isn't supplied (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253 and :315)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback branch is only used when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then does `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined, this comparison cannot match any normal calendar with a string externalId, so the lookup will return undefined. This makes the destinationCalendar-based fallback effectively dead/unreachable and can cause the code to fall back to "primary" (or pass undefined) even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId. This is visible at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around the changed lines ~253 and ~312.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 credential fetch plus sequential event creation loop in createAllCalendarEvents: awaiting createEvent() sequentially per destination and doing per-iteration prisma.credential.findUnique causes N sequential external calendar API calls and N individual DB round-trips on the booking-creation critical path instead of batching (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~334-385)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and (a) may `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside the loop when the credential isn’t already in `this.calendarCredentials`, and (b) then `await createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` inside the same loop. This makes both DB lookups and calendar API calls run sequentially per destination (and potentially one DB round-trip per destination), rather than batching or parallelizing via `Promise.all`. That is a verifiable N+1/sequential-on-critical-path performance issue introduced by the diff when multiple destination calendars are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same N+1 shape in updateAllCalendarEvents: sequential await prisma.credential.findUnique inside the reference.credentialId branch for every calendar reference serializes DB round-trips across references instead of batching up front (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~493-525)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the updated updateAllCalendarEvents logic now iterates `for (const reference of calendarReference)` and, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside that loop. Because this is a sequential `await` within the loop, multiple calendar references will trigger multiple DB round-trips serialized one after another rather than being batched or parallelized. This is a verifiable N+1/performance issue introduced by the new per-reference fetching logic (~493-525).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recurring-event deletion cascade multiplied per reference: the recurring-cancellation block now executes once per calendar reference inside the for loop, issuing up to K× the external delete API calls for collective bookings with K hosts, risking Google API quota consumption and rate limits (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~415-470)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from `find` (single calendar reference) to `filter` (array) and wraps the whole deletion logic in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that loop, the recurring-event deletion branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) runs a `map` over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` and then iterates `updatedBookings` to delete events. That inner deletion logic does not depend on the specific `reference` being iterated, so executing it once per reference will multiply the same set of delete calls by the number of calendar references, potentially issuing K× duplicate external deletes and consuming quota/rate limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fan-out duplication when destination entries lack credentialId: every destination entry without a credentialId triggers event creation on all credentials of that integration type, so multiple destination entries lacking credentialId create duplicate calendar events and redundant API calls (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~370-376)

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the new loop iterates over every entry in event.destinationCalendar. For entries without destination.credentialId, it executes the `else` branch that filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then calls `createEvent(c, event)` for *all* matching credentials. If there are multiple destination entries lacking credentialId (especially with the same integration), this same “all credentials of that type” creation runs multiple times, producing duplicate calendar events and redundant API calls. This behavior is directly implied by the loop structure and the per-destination fan-out logic added in the diff (around ~370-376).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent 'primary' fallback in Google createEvent when no credential matches: selectedCalendar falls back to 'primary' when no destination entry matches the passed credentialId, writing multi-host events to the wrong primary calendar instead of surfacing a mismatch (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~146-150)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale or undefined credential leaked across reference loop iterations in updateAllCalendarEvents because credential is declared outside the for loop, causing updates to the wrong host's calendar or throwing and aborting all remaining references

Also, the `else` branch uses `for (const credential of credentials)` which shadows the outer `credential` variable, so it doesn’t reuse the previous iteration’s value either. adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find predicate compares cal.externalId against undefined/null and never matches, so calendarId becomes undefined and Google API calls fail on reschedule/cancel (CalendarService.ts:253-256, 314-316)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` the fallback branch is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact condition to enter the fallback), the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to `undefined`/`null`, so it will not match any normal destination calendar (which should have a real `externalId`). That makes `selectedCalendar` `undefined`, effectively breaking the intended fallback to a destination calendar.

The same incorrect pattern exists in `deleteEvent`:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

So the finding correctly identifies a real logic bug introduced by the diff: the fallback cannot ever select a valid destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, leading to wrong/undefined `calendarId` usage (or unintended fallback to `primary` if applied later).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/self-negating fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent: the else branch predicate 'cal.externalId === externalCalendarId' compares against undefined/null and can never match, so find() always returns undefined, silently removing the previous event.destinationCalendar?.externalId fallback (should likely find by credentialId as done in createEvent); same pattern duplicated in deleteEvent

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email in createEvent uses mainHostDestinationCalendar (first destination calendar at index [0]) instead of selectedCalendar, so in collective events with multiple Google hosts the organizer email will be host #1's calendar ID even when the event is created on host #2's calendar

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent` now supports multiple destination calendars by selecting the target `calendarId` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` (so the insert happens on the calendar matching the passed credential). However, the organizer attendee email is derived from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first element of the destinationCalendar array):

```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.length ? calEventRaw.destinationCalendar : [];
...
email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email
```

This means when multiple destination calendars exist (e.g., collective events with multiple Google hosts), events created for host #2 (selected by `credentialId`) will still set the organizer attendee email based on host #1’s destination calendar externalId. That is a concrete mismatch introduced by the diff and can lead to incorrect organizer/attendee identity on those events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy so the find predicate cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making calendarId undefined and causing canceled bookings to leave orphaned events and edits/reschedules to fail

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id like:

```ts
externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

When the `else` branch runs, `externalCalendarId` is falsy (typically `undefined`/`null`), so the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will almost never match any real calendar (their `externalId` should be a non-empty string). That makes the lookup effectively dead, producing `undefined`.

Consequences visible in the diff:
- `updateEvent`: `selectedCalendar` can become `undefined`, which is an invalid `calendarId` for Google API and can break updates/reschedules.
- `deleteEvent`: the same pattern can yield `undefined`, and the function defines `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so it may fall back to deleting from the wrong calendar (leaving the actual event orphaned).

This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking references lose externalCalendarId for the no-credentialId path because createAllCalendarEvents else-branch calls createEvent with no externalId, so stored references have externalCalendarId undefined and later mutations fail

Silent skip when a destination's credential can't be resolved (credentialFromDB null, deleted, or app.slug null): no EventResult pushed, no error logged, so booking is reported successful while a host's calendar never receives the event

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the branch `if (destination.credentialId)` attempts to resolve a credential from `this.calendarCredentials`, else fetches from DB. If `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` returns null, or returns a record without `app.slug`, `credential` remains undefined and the code simply falls through without pushing an `EventResult` and without logging. Because `event.destinationCalendar` is non-empty, it also bypasses the fallback `else` that would create events on other calendars, so this can return `createdEvents` missing (or empty) for that destination with no explicit failure surfaced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In updateAllCalendarEvents, a failed DB fetch passes credential = undefined into updateEvent which throws in getCalendar, and the outer catch converts all references into failures discarding ones that already succeeded (cascade failure)

adjudication.rationale: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (EventManager.ts), inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set, the code tries to find the credential in `this.calendarCredentials`, and if not found tries a DB fetch. However, if the DB fetch returns null/undefined, `credential` remains undefined and the code still executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` with no guard. That can throw (e.g., in `updateEvent`/`getCalendar` when accessing credential fields). The whole method is wrapped in a `try/catch`, and the `catch` returns a mapped failure for *all* calendar references, so one missing credential can cause the function to report all references as failed (and also drop any accumulated `result`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reschedule-merge deletion path still uses .find() on booking.references instead of .filter(), so only the first old calendar reference is deleted and hosts 2..N keep stale events after a reschedule

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the code was updated to treat calendar references as an array (`calendarReference = ...filter(...)`) and to update all of them, but the reschedule/merge cleanup still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`. If there are multiple `_calendar` references (now possible with `destinationCalendar` being an array and multiple events created), this `find()` will only select one old reference to delete, leaving other old calendar events undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email forced to mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId (first destination) for all hosts' calendars in Google createEvent/updateEvent, causing rejected inserts or wrong organizer attribution on secondary hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` and `updateEvent` now derive `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as the *first* entry of `destinationCalendar` and use its `externalId` to set the organizer attendee `email`:

- `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : ...`

But the actual `calendarId` used for insertion is selected by matching the passed `credentialId`:

- `const selectedCalendar = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;`

So when creating/updating events for a non-first destination calendar (secondary host), the payload still stamps the organizer attendee email based on the first destination calendar’s `externalId`, not the calendar corresponding to the current credential. That mismatch is directly present in the diff and can lead to incorrect organizer attribution and potentially API issues if `externalId` is not a valid email for that credential/calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB credential fetches in EventManager look up credentials by bare id with no ownership check against the booking's users, a potential credential-abuse vector if any API lets users write destinationCalendar.credentialId

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new fallbacks in `EventManager` that call `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` (and similarly for `reference.credentialId`) when the credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`. That lookup is by bare primary key only, with no constraint that the credential belongs to the booking/user/team associated with this `EventManager` instance. If an attacker can influence `destinationCalendar.credentialId` / calendar reference `credentialId` (directly or via stored booking data), this code would use an arbitrary credential record, enabling cross-tenant credential misuse. Even aside from attacker control, it can incorrectly bind to an unrelated credential if IDs are wrong, because there’s no ownership validation.
